subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as a core `bootstrap-extra-files` startup-context contract?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally constrain extra bootstrap injection to known workspace filenames, while the requested behavior expands deterministic system-prompt context loading and changes user-facing hook semantics.

options.title: Approve guarded custom files
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the linked PR or replacement preserves containment guards, budgets, diagnostics, session filtering, docs, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames
options.body: Leave `bootstrap-extra-files` limited to known workspace filenames and direct users to first-class bootstrap files or explicit reads for custom context.

options.title: Defer to broader context design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers choose a broader context/discovery API that covers custom startup files without adding one-off hook semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom files
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the linked PR or replacement preserves containment guards, budgets, diagnostics, session filtering, docs, and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history on the bundled hook and boundary-safe workspace read surfaces and was mentioned in the issue timeline for maintainer attention.
